string-array.name: story_starters_mystery
string-array.item: The grandfather clock struck thirteen, and the locked study door slowly creaked open.
A single wet footprint lay in the center of the dry parlor floor, leading nowhere.
The letter had no return address, only three words: \'They found it.\'
Professor Vance was dead, but the chess game in his office had just progressed by one move.
The lighthouse lamp went out, not from a broken bulb, but because someone had painted it black.
Every mirror in the mansion had been covered with a black veil, save for the one in the attic.
She opened her locker to find a key she had never seen before, tagged with her own name.
A dog barked at the empty wall for hours until the plaster began to crack.
He bought the antique desk at an auction, only to find a secret compartment holding a diary dated tomorrow.
The train passengers woke up to find the dining car completely empty, but the table was set for twelve.

string-array.name: story_starters_fantasy
string-array.item: The sword in the stone didn\'t pull loose; instead, it began to whisper in a language long forgotten.
Every time it rained, the puddles in the village square showed a reflection of a different sky.
She was born with a shadow that didn\'t match her movements, but rather followed a silent stranger.
The old map didn\'t show roads or rivers, but instead marked where the dragons used to sleep.
A glowing blue flower bloomed on the kitchen table overnight, feeding on the family\'s secrets.
He traded his last copper coin for a bottle of starlight, hoping it would guide him through the Whispering Woods.
The forest trees began to migrate south, leaving behind ancient ruins that weren\'t there yesterday.
She wore a necklace of tiny glass beads, each holding the memory of a storm.
The king\'s crown grew heavier with every lie he spoke, until it began to crush his brow.
In the city of cloud-weavers, the wind suddenly refused to carry their threads.

string-array.name: story_starters_scifi
string-array.item: The distress signal had been traveling through space for a thousand years, using a human voice.
His new artificial eye worked perfectly, except it occasionally displayed a countdown timer in the corner.
The terraforming colony woke up to find that the barren red sand had turned into blue grass overnight.
Her ship\'s AI began to draft poetry about a planet that did not exist on any map.
A massive chrome cylinder descended from the sky, hovering silently over the ocean without making a ripple.
The chronometer ticked backwards for three seconds, and everyone on the station felt a sudden chill.
They built the perfect virtual reality, but someone forgot to code an exit button.
The capsule retrieved from the black hole contained a single, perfectly fresh apple.
In the year 2142, sleep was no longer natural; it had to be downloaded as a software patch.
He discovered that his reflection in the smart-mirror was lagging behind by exactly five minutes.

string-array.name: story_starters_drama
string-array.item: After twenty years of silence, the phone on the bedside table rang, and her father\'s voice spoke.
He packed his life into a single suitcase, leaving the keys on the kitchen counter next to the ring.
The small-town bakery was famous for its bread, but the secret ingredient was a century-old promise.
She sat on the park bench every Tuesday, waiting for the man who would never return.
A box of old letters found in the attic revealed that their family home was never actually theirs.
He looked at the painting he had worked on for ten years and realized it was time to paint over it.
The letter of acceptance arrived the same day they received the eviction notice.
She found her childhood diary in the bookstore\'s discount bin, with pages added in someone else\'s handwriting.
They stood under the awning as the summer rain poured, both too proud to say the first apology.
The stage curtain rose, but the lead actor stood completely still, staring at the empty front row.
